options: A shroud around the propeller that increases thrust at low speed
A valve on the sea chest
questions.explanation: It improves bollard pull, which is why tugs use it.

options: A recess or box in the hull that supplies sea water for cooling and other systems
questions.explanation: It usually has a grating and a way to clear it.

options: Cools the fuel in the day tank
Cools engine fresh water by passing it through pipes fixed outside the hull
questions.explanation: No raw-water intake is needed, so there is less fouling and corrosion inside the engine.

options: Has blade pitch that cannot be changed while in service
Can be adjusted from the bridge

questions.stem: Seacocks should be operated regularly because:
options: They can seize in the open position if never moved, and fail to close when needed
The rules say they should be painted yearly
questions.explanation: A seized valve cannot isolate a failed hose.

questions.stem: The engine overheats and the raw-water pump is turning normally. A likely cause is:
options: A blocked sea strainer, for example with kelp or jellyfish
questions.explanation: Weed or jellyfish in the strainer restricts the flow of cooling water.

questions.stem: Before opening a sea strainer that sits below the waterline you must:
options: Open the drain on the fuel tank
questions.explanation: Otherwise sea water will flood in when the lid comes off.

questions.stem: A sacrificial anode protects a propeller by:
options: Corroding in preference to it, because the anode metal is more reactive
questions.explanation: The anode is the weaker metal in the galvanic pair and wastes away instead of the propeller.

questions.stem: You should not paint a sacrificial anode because:
options: The colour would affect the compass
Paint would stop it making good electrical contact with the water, so it would not protect
questions.explanation: An anode must be bare metal to work.

questions.stem: A rubber hose on an overboard fitting bursts and water floods in. A prompt action is to:
options: Close the seacock, or drive a bung into the opening if you cannot, and tell the master
Switch off the bilge pump to save power
questions.explanation: Stop the water at the hull opening first, then call the master and use the pumps.
